addition.item: Box on the administrator home page (module in position cpanel): traffic light of the Cloudflare connection, button to clear the whole cache, field to clear one or more addresses, outcome of the last purge. Shown to Super Users and the user groups chosen in the options; checked on the server on every call.

Guided setup in the plugin options: where to find the Zone ID, how to create the token, and a Verify connection button that checks token, zone and purge permission and explains in plain words what is wrong; with the optional Zone Read permission it finds the Zone ID by itself.
Purge mode: the whole cache (default) or only the changed addresses (article, categories, home page, fixed extra addresses), the old address too when an article is renamed or moved.
New events, each with its own switch: categories, menu items, site modules, custom fields and tags; optionally also System > Clear Cache.
Italian language files; log file with the outcome of every purge (no token, no Zone ID).

Joomla Web Services API: a program (for example a bot that publishes articles) can clear the Cloudflare cache with the Joomla API token of a user: GET /api/index.php/v1/cfpurge/status, POST /api/index.php/v1/cfpurge/all, POST /api/index.php/v1/cfpurge/urls. Who may do it is set with the new permissions of the component Cloudflare Cache Purge (Read the state, Clear the cache), by user group; Super Users always can; nobody else until you grant it. The answers never contain the Cloudflare token or the Zone ID. Same checks and limits as the box on the administrator home page. Close the API by switching off the plugin Web Services - Cloudflare Cache Purge.

change.item: The plugin is now part of the package pkg_cfpurge (content plugin, system plugin, administrator module). Installing it over 1.1.4, or updating from System > Update, keeps Zone ID, token and switches. After the upgrade click Verify connection once to enable the buttons of the box.
A purge refused by Cloudflare is no longer treated as done: it is logged and shown in the box. The purge is sent once at the end of the request, in blocks of 30 addresses, with an 8 second timeout.
Version 2.0.0 was built but never published: 2.1.0 is the first release of the package and contains everything of it.
The package now also contains the API component (com_cfpurge) and the Web Services plugin (plg_webservices_cfpurge).

addition.item: Cloudflare Cache Purge is now a package (pkg_cfpurge) with a box on the administrator home page, a guided setup with a Verify connection button, a targeted purge mode, more events (categories, menu items, modules, custom fields, tags, System > Clear Cache) and Italian language files. This update installs the package over the plugin: Zone ID, token and switches are kept. It also adds the Joomla Web Services API for programs (permissions in the Options of the component Cloudflare Cache Purge). After the update open the plugin options and click Verify connection once, to enable the buttons of the box.

fix.item: Event switches now render correctly as ON (green) by default: fixed the switcher option order (No/Yes) so the toggle position matches the stored value. No change in behaviour, purge is on for all events by default.

change.item: JED Checker compliance: en-GB language files (sys.ini/ini), manifest name follows the "{Type} - {Name}" convention, removed the non-standard <icon> element, control-character filter rewritten without hex escapes (JAMSS-clean). No functional changes.
JED compliance: English UI labels and description, GPL licence header in every PHP file, extension name aligned with the JED listing. No functional changes.

addition.item: Plugin icon bundled in the package and shown in the Joomla Extensions manager.

feature.item: Four independent switches to choose which events trigger the purge: article create, update, state change (publish/unpublish/trash) and delete. All on by default.

security.item: Defensive hardening: rawurlencode of the zone in the API URL and stripping of control characters from the token (anti header-injection).
SHA-256 integrity hash added to the update server so Joomla verifies the downloaded package.

addition.item: Joomla Update System integration for one-click updates.

note.item: First release: purge the Cloudflare cache on article save / state change / delete.
